title: Research: charged common-A broadcast readout (no new kappa)
body:
## Result

Adds a bounded common-A broadcast-readout construction for the five-source dirty connector. With one common exact F2-linear output map A, the fixed ten-toggle witness covers all 31 nonzero target masks using 10 A evaluations and 64 target-row updates. The same witness in the existing single-target alphabet uses 64 A evaluations and 64 target updates.

This is one explicitly priced operation extension: R_S computes A z once and adds the result to every listed dirty target. It changes the output-map hypothesis to A_i = A and preserves arbitrary dirty sources, connector, and targets.

## Complete cost comparison

The package separates the full A evaluation, per-target row update, and control/routing costs:

    C_unicast   = P + 2 sum_j b_j + 64(a + w) + D_u
    C_broadcast = P + 2 sum_j b_j + 10 a + 64 w + D_b
    saving      = 54 a + D_u - D_b

All 64 target writes remain charged. The construction helps exactly when D_b - D_u < 54a. Its dense F2 reference implementation streams each A-output coordinate through one scalar accumulator, needs no extra full-length row, and lists the complete arithmetic, data and program-bit counts in the certificate. No supplier admission or new kappa is claimed.

## Verification

- Pinned predecessor control: PASS_UNIVERSAL_CONNECTOR_BOUNDARY pairings=945 max_coverage=31 queries=74 leaves=182
- New construction: PASS_COMMON_A_BROADCAST small_basis_columns=18 masks=31 source_calls=10 distinct_states=10 A_evaluations=10 ordinary_A_calls=64 target_writes=64 descriptor_bits=680->450 dense_basis_columns=111 random_dirty_cases=96 negative_controls=3
- Package source pins and metadata: PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS
- Registered replay: PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE under CPython 3.12.15
- Optimized verifier invocation also passes.

## Provenance and limits

Base commit: 0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea. Selected-record SHA-256: 10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32.

The package credits Ross Richardson's PR943 for the source-prefix witness and CubeJerry's PR889 for related common-right-factor batching. It differs by sharing a common output-side A across changing source-prefix states. The open DUO/triple-sum work changes source calls and remains separate.

The result is a finite interface construction with a fully stated break-even condition. It does not show that the selected supplier exposes a common A, realize the construction in the selected recursive word, or change the selected result. The review, source manifest, assembly certificate, and reproduction command are pinned in SOURCES.json and README.md. Substantial OpenAI Codex/GPT-6 assistance is disclosed in TASK.json.
